name: American Wheat
title: American Wheat Beer: Style Guide | Craft Beer School
desc: American wheat beer explained: soft wheat, clean yeast and light hops, why it tastes nothing like a hefeweizen, and what to eat with it in India.
tagline: Wheat beer with the banana and clove taken out: soft, bready, lightly hoppy and easy.
tastes:
If you have had a German hefeweizen, this is the beer that looks similar and tastes quite different. American brewers use a big share of wheat malt for the soft body and pale haze, but ferment with a clean ale yeast. So there is no banana, no clove, just bread dough, a little honey and whatever the hops bring.

That hop character can be gentle and floral or quite citrusy, depending on the brewery. Bitterness stays low to moderate. Some versions are filtered and clear, others left hazy; both are fine.

The style became common in American brewpubs in the 1980s and 1990s as a friendly first craft beer, and it plays that role well. It is often the base for fruit beers too, because a clean wheat beer does not clash with mango, watermelon or berries the way a spicy hefeweizen can.

profile.look: Pale straw to light gold, clear or with a soft haze. A white, fluffy head that lasts.
profile.aroma_flavour: Fresh bread, light honey and grain from the wheat. Clean fermentation with no banana or clove. Low to moderate hop aroma, floral or citrus.
profile.mouthfeel: Light to medium body, soft and smooth from the wheat, lively carbonation and a dry finish.
profile.ingredients: Thirty to fifty per cent wheat malt with pale barley malt. American hops such as Cascade or Willamette. A clean American ale yeast, never a weizen strain.

in_india: American wheat is an easy fit for Indian weather: light, soft, not too bitter and fine to drink cold on a hot afternoon. It is also a sensible beer for a crowd at a wedding or a cricket match, because it does not demand much of anyone. Wheat beers go stale faster than lagers, so buy fresh and keep it chilled. Brewers here often use it as the base for mango or jamun seasonals.

pairings.why: The bready wheat matches the buttered pav, and the bubbles clean up the spiced butter.
A light, clean beer lets the carom and gram flour batter shine while scrubbing the oil off your palate.
Tamarind, onion and crunch need a gentle beer that will not fight the sweet and sour chutneys.
Ripe mango and a clean wheat beer are a natural match, which is why so many fruit beers start here.
